meta.title: Charms & Curses
meta.description: The 17 Charms and 26 Curses you can hold during a run: what each one does, how effects scale with the number of items you hold, and where the items come from (Dark Deals, Minibosses, the Shrine and the Lab). The systems are identical between Vanilla and EX apart from one cap on the Grace pair and the all-caps item names in Vanilla.

prose.heading: Passive items with a twist
prose.text: Charms and Curses are passive items that sit in your bag and modify your run — you never 'equip' them. Charms point the effect at you; Curses are its mirror image, pointed at your opponents. When you hold both sides of the same effect, they net against each other — the diagram below works the Catching pair through the math.

prose.heading: How strong is a stack?
prose.text: Most chance effects stack linearly per item and cap at 90%, so holding more past the cap buys nothing — the chart plots each capped effect. STAB, Strength, Catching, Wild and Crit scale per item with their own caps (or none); status items like Torment, Pressure and Unaware don't scale at all — one is all you need. The game keeps a live count of each effect and recalculates whenever your bag changes.

prose.heading: Where you get them
prose.text: There is no shop for Charms and Curses during a run — every source is in-run luck or a trade.
list: Dark Deal (graveyard), the main source: three random Charms on offer, take one, and the salesman 'afflicts' you with a random Curse as the price.
Mysterious Shrine: trades the one-time Sacred Ash for a Capacity Curse.
Miniboss encounters: normal random items only — the random pool never holds a Charm or a Curse.
The Lab: one of Birch's rescued Pokémon may be holding a random Curse — a quarter early on, 40% by the mid-Gyms, 60% in the Elite Four phase, certain at Champion difficulty.
prose.trailing: Vanilla builds show all of these item names in ALL CAPS (e.g. GRACE CHARM); EX shows them in title case.

records.name: Strength Charm
records.description: Pokémon you catch come out stronger: after netting against any Strength Curses, each net charm sets a floor of 20 on all six of a caught Pokémon's IVs (up to 31 per IV) — one net charm means every IV is 20 or better, two net charms max them out.

records.name: Catching Charm
records.description: Ball effectiveness is increased by 200% per item held — the single biggest catch-rate booster — netted against any Catching Curses.

records.name: Grace Charm
records.description: Your moves' secondary effects — the chance of a burn, poison, flinch or stat drop — become more likely: the odds are multiplied by (100 + the stacked bonus) / 100, so one Grace Charm makes them 1.75× as likely, and each further charm adds on top. The bonus cap is the one real mechanical difference between versions: Vanilla caps it at 90 (1.9× from two charms on), EX raises it to 150 (2.5× from two charms on).

differences.vanilla: Stacked grace is capped at 90 (min(count × 75, 90)): 1.75× with one charm, 1.9× with two or more — only a third and later charm adds nothing.
differences.ex: Stacked grace is capped at 150 (min(count × 75, 150)): 1.75× with one charm, 2.5× with two or more.

records.name: Sacred Ash
records.description: A one-time run insurance item: if your entire party faints, it shines, revives all of your Pokémon and teleports you back to the adventure path for a second chance. It is consumed when it triggers. The Mysterious Shrine is the main source, traded against a Capacity Curse.

records.name: Retry Charm
records.description: The permanent version of the Sacred Ash: your whole party revives and the run rewinds to the path overview every time you wipe — with no item consumed. Effectively infinite extra lives.
